finding: The 0.0% targeted balance_engine score was a MEASUREMENT-TOOLCHAIN artefact, not a test-quality gap.
root_cause: mutmut 3.7.0 get_mutant_name() strips a leading 'src.' from path-derived mutant module names. This repository imports production code as 'src.<package>'. The mutated-file trampoline compares mutmut's stripped name against decorated_func.__module__ and, on mismatch, calls the ORIGINAL function. With a pristine install every mutant is therefore dispatched to unmutated code, so the test suite passes for every mutant and the campaign reports 0.0% with all mutants 'survived'.

control_pristine.note: Control run deliberately stopped once 74/74 mutants had been dispatched to the original function; the trend is 0 killed / 74 survived, identical to GitHub run 36238247482 (0.0%, 285 survived).

conclusion: Identical population (285 mutants) and identical selection: 0.0%/285 survived under a pristine toolchain vs 95.4%/13 survived under the contract-conformant toolchain. The declared dependency contract (pip install -e '.[all]') and the working toolchain are now the same thing, enforced and audited by runtime/foundation/verification/mutmut_contract.py.

prior_classification_correction.authority: C71 controlled experiment + mutmut 3.7.0 source (utils/format_utils.py get_mutant_name; mutation/trampoline.py dispatch)
